body:
## Why

A card's `kb.model`, and the `model` on the profile its `kb:agent:*` label names, are **silently ignored for every node of a track**. The board states one model and the work runs on another.

Measured on this board, 2026-09-02 (track #288, nodes #289-#293). The `claude` profile is `claude-sonnet-5`; every node ran `claude-opus-5`, read from the subagent sidecar transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<runner-session>/subagents/`:

| node | model in its transcript |
|---|---|
| #289 | `claude-opus-5` ×262 |
| #290 | `claude-opus-5` ×299 |
| #291 | `claude-opus-5` ×201 |
| #292 / #293 | `claude-opus-5` ×32 / ×31 |

Not one Sonnet turn. The runner itself was launched `--model claude-opus-5` (its `claude-track` profile), and the subagents inherited it, because a subagent with no model of its own runs on its parent's.

Three independent causes, each sufficient on its own:

1. **The model only ever reaches a worker through the launch line.** `spawnWorker` sets `vars.model = task.kb.model || profile.model` (`src/dispatch.js`), `expandLaunch` substitutes `{model_args}`, `modelArgs` (`src/model.js`) emits `--model <m>`.
2. **A track node has no launch line.** `spawnWorker` runs once per track, for the root, on the root's profile. Nodes are `Agent` subagents inside that session, so the substitution never runs for them.
3. **The runner is neither told the node's model nor asked to pass one.** `trackContext({repo, board, track, attempt, waves, fanout, trackBranch, defaultBranch})` (`src/track.js`) takes no profiles and no board config; `nodeLine` prints number, status, agent, priority, title, paths — no model; and the fan-out instruction names only the `Agent` tool, `isolation: "worktree"` and the prompt.

The capability is there and unused: the `Agent` tool takes a `model`, and Claude Code's own subagent definitions (`.claude/agents/*.md`) take a `model:` in frontmatter. hkb names neither.

Cost, plainly: a board that sets a cheap model for nodes and a strong one for the orchestrator pays the orchestrator's rate for everything. And `hkb stats` cannot price subagents (the sidecar transcript is not the attempt's `transcript_path`), so none of it shows up on the board afterwards either.

## What

The shape to build is two configurable levels, which is what a reader of the board already expects it to mean:

- **the runner** — one session, one model: the track profile's own `model` (`claude-track` → opus today). This already works.
- **the node** — its own subagent, its own model: `kb.model` on the card, else the node's profile `model`, else a track-profile default for its nodes, else inherit the runner's.

Concretely:

1. **Resolve it.** A pure `nodeModel(node, cfg, runnerProfile)` in `src/track.js` (unit-tested) returning the first of: `node.kb.model` · `cfg.profiles[node.agent]?.model` · `runnerProfile.node_model` (new, optional — a track profile's default for the nodes it runs, so "orchestrate on opus, work on sonnet" is one line of board.json) · `null` meaning inherit.
2. **Carry it into the brief.** `trackContext` gains the board config — its one caller, `src/dispatch.js`, already holds `ctx.cfg` — and `nodeLine` prints the resolved model per node.
3. **Ask for it.** The fan-out instruction tells the runner to pass `model: "<m>"` in that node's `Agent` call when the brief names one, and to omit the field when it does not, so inheriting stays the default.
4. **Say what a harness without subagents cannot do.** `trackFanout` is `true` exactly when the profile's effective tools include `Agent` — so the two briefs are "this harness has subagents" and "it does not", **not** concurrent versus serial. A node that must wait for its blocker still gets its own subagent, just started later, and still carries its own model. Only a runner with no `Agent` at all (Copilot CLI, Codex) runs nodes inside its own session, and there a per-node model cannot exist. The sequential brief should say that in one line instead of implying the profile applies; `hkb track <root>` should name it as a cost of that mode.
5. **Doctor.** A track whose nodes name a model their runner will not apply is worth one `!` line: the root, the nodes, and which of the two briefs it is on.

Keep out of scope: pricing subagent usage in `hkb stats` (that is the separate sidecar-transcript gap), and changing any default model.

## Done when

- [ ] `nodeModel` resolves in the documented order, with a unit test per rung including "absent means inherit".
- [ ] `nodeLine` prints the resolved model, and the fan-out brief tells the runner to pass `model:` for a node that has one and to omit it for a node that does not — asserted both ways.
- [ ] `node_model` on a track profile is accepted by `loadBoard` and documented beside `track_agents`; an unknown value is refused at load like `effort` is.
- [ ] The sequential brief states in one line that a per-node model cannot be honoured without subagents, and says why.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green; `docs/wiki/features/tracks.md` gains the paragraph.

## Contract

Do not change any default model, and do not make hkb pass `model:` for a node that resolves to none — inheriting the runner's model stays the default and is today's behaviour. The `Agent` tool's field is `model`, alongside `isolation` and the prompt. `runner.model` is not a new key: it is the track profile's existing `model`.
goal: a node with kb.model or a profile model runs on it inside a fan-out track; the sequential brief says plainly that it cannot
title: A track node ignores its card's and profile's model — every node runs on the runner's
